scenes.headline: Ranking
scenes.subtitle: Assigning positions to rows within a window.
scenes.narration: Ranking functions assign a position to each row within an ordered window, such as first, second, and third.

scenes.headline: Ranking functions
items: row_number gives a unique sequential position
dense_rank leaves no gaps after ties
All require an ordered window specification
scenes.narration: The row_number function gives each row a unique sequential position. Rank leaves gaps after ties, dense_rank leaves no gaps, and all of them require an ordered window specification to work.

scenes.headline: Top item per group
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

w = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(F.desc("sales"))
top = df.withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w)).filter("rn = 1")
scenes.narration: We define a window per category ordered by descending sales, then use row_number to number rows within each category. Filtering for row number equal to one gives the single best-selling item in every category.

scenes.headline: rank vs dense_rank
scenes.narration: With rank, tied rows share a number and the next rank skips ahead, producing gaps like one, one, three. Dense_rank also ties but never skips, producing one, one, two.

scenes.text: Use row_number for a strict top-N and dense_rank when ties should count equally.
scenes.narration: Choose row_number for a strict top-N and dense_rank when tied rows should genuinely count as the same position.
